To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the presheaf of partial orders is a model of concurrent computation, (2) event structures with symmetry represent all presheafs over finite partial orders, (3) graded event structures with strong symmetry represent precisely all the presheaves over partial orders that are separated.

(i) the category of event structure with symmetry and the category of preshaves over finite partial order are equivalent, and (ii) the category of separated event structures with symmetry and the subcategory corresponding to separated presheaves are equivalent.
(a) the class of event structures with strong symmetry is a model of all separated presheaves; and (b) the class of symmetric event structures is a model of the class of all presheaves.
